notes: Real-repository corpus (internal/corpus). v3 gives the corpus GO DEPTH: six pinned Go repositories (uuid, lo, cobra, gin, grpc-go, kubernetes) carry the P0 FR-2 stratification, beside the five non-Go repositories kept for cross-language regression detection (flask, sinatra, ky, express, guava). Refs pin RELEASE TAGS; sha additionally pins the checkout HEAD (case-insensitive prefix, >=12 hex chars — the Go entries pin the FULL 40-char commit sha). If an upstream tag is ever re-pointed, the pin step fails closed. Every count under `measured` was taken from a real clone at the pinned sha on the recorded date, never from repository metadata; `go_files` is the strict count the stress threshold is asserted on. Tiers: 1 = PR gate (local fixtures), 2 = pinned SHAs, 3 = nightly/manual, 4 = manual-only stress (corpus.yml caps the scheduled run at -max-tier 3, so tier 4 never runs on a schedule or a PR). Adding a repository is a data change here, never a code change. Per-repository selection rationale: corpus/README.md.

stratification.evidence: 21 Go files in a single package, 31 tracked files — the smallest real repository in the corpus.
36 Go files in 2 packages; the CLI framework plus its doc generator, with 17 test files.
92 Go files in 7 packages; HTTP router, middleware chain, binding and render subpackages.
831 Go files spread over 277 directories containing Go source.
15718 Go files over 3611 package directories; staging/ alone holds 5899 of them as separately published modules.
13 of 17 Go files declare type-parameterised functions over any/comparable constraints.

11 go.mod files (root plus examples, interop, security, stats and cmd submodules). Asserted on grpc-go rather than kubernetes (34 go.mod) because grpc-go runs on the nightly tier, so the property is exercised without the stress target.
16 Go files carry //go:build constraints (nomsgpack, jsoniter, sonic, go1.20+ variants).
49 Go files carry the "Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT" marker (protobuf and grpc plugin output).
287 _test.go files, 13 of which declare Benchmark functions.

entries.name: cobra
entries.permitted_use: Public repository under Apache-2.0; the corpus shallow-clones it read-only in CI and publishes measurements only — no source is redistributed.

measured.method: git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.8.0; git ls-files '*.go' | wc -l and git ls-files | wc -l at the pinned sha

entries.notes: Go CLI framework; the typeresolve (v0.2.0) acceptance target. The confirmed_edges assertion is the acceptance gate: Command.Execute calls c.ExecuteC() — a receiver-method dispatch the name heuristic cannot prove — and the go/types pass must carry it at the confirmed tier. v3 widened the sha pin from the 12-char prefix to the full commit sha; the tag and the assertion are unchanged.

The second search asserts RouterGroup rather than the more obvious Context: `graphi search Context` returns no matches on ANY indexed repository (observed on gin and kubernetes, 2026-07-27) — a search-side observation recorded in SW-122, not a property of this repository.

entries.notes: The FR-2 stress target: 15718 Go files (>= the 10000 threshold) across 3611 package directories and 34 modules. Tier 4 — deliberately outside BOTH the PR gate and the nightly schedule: a measured full index costs ~3m16s wall and ~9 GB peak RSS on an 8-core laptop (2026-07-27, v0.6.7 dev build), which no hosted runner should absorb on a schedule. Run it explicitly: `go run ./cmd/corpus -manifest corpus/manifest.json -tier 4` or `go run ./cmd/eval -full-run kubernetes` once SW-123 has named a runner class and SW-124 the budgets.
